key_facts: most severe sweating at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previous treatment with 20% aluminum chloride for axillary hyperhidrosis
unsuccessful treatment with aluminum chloride for intergluteal cleft and sacrum
uses absorbent pads due to severity of condition
unable to attend work due to condition
Minor starch-iodine test performed to localize areas of overactive sweating
significant sweating identified in sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area)

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of axillary hyperhidrosis and now presents with excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, which are typical areas affected by primary focal hyperhidrosis. The Minor starch-iodine test confirmed significant sweating in these areas.

rejected.label: Compensatory hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: There is no indication of another area of the body having decreased sweating to compensate for the increased sweating in the buttocks.

rejected.label: Eccrine nevus
rejected.why: No mention of a congenital anomaly or nevus-related symptoms.

rejected.label: Secondary hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: No underlying medical condition or medication is mentioned that could be causing the hyperhidrosis.

rejected.label: Chronic idiopathic axillary hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: The patient's condition is not limited to the axillary region, as he also experiences excessive sweating in the buttocks.

rejected.label: Gustatory sweating
rejected.why: The sweating is not triggered by eating or tasting food.

rejected.label: Freud syndrome
rejected.why: No association with auriculotemporal nerve damage or trauma.

rejected.label: Frey syndrome
rejected.why: No history of parotid gland surgery or trauma.

rejected.label: Harlequin syndrome
rejected.why: No mention of flushing or sweating affecting one side of the face or body.

rejected.label: Ross syndrome
rejected.why: No indication of adrenal insufficiency or other symptoms associated with this condition.

rejected.label: Generalized dysautonomia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are localized to specific areas, rather than a generalized autonomic dysfunction.
